name: pdo-control
description: PDO PostgreSQL control on PHP's pdo_pgsql. No Laravel and no pool. correct rolls back after a caught statement error because PDO exposes no transaction status and no command tag. unsafe treats a true PDO::commit() as success and keeps the handle when PDO::rollBack() throws. persistent is the correct policy with PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT. Category C faults withhold PDO::rollBack() once, before pdo_pgsql sends. TX-01B.commit-reply-discarded is not implemented: pdo_pgsql consumes the COMMIT reply inside commit().

modes.description: Positive control. PDO::beginTransaction, prepared inserts, then PDO::commit or PDO::rollBack. A caught statement error calls rollBack() and does not call commit(). A thrown rollBack() or commit() drops the handle and is reported as failed, not as a confirmed rollback. ATTR_PERSISTENT is false. One connection, not a pool. The command tag is not read.

Negative control. PDO::commit() returning true is reported as committed, including after a caught unique violation. A thrown commit() is reported as rolled_back. A thrown rollBack() keeps the handle. The next unit continues on that handle when beginTransaction reports an active transaction. ATTR_PERSISTENT is false.
The correct completion policy with PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT true. TX-03 only, plus the observation controls. Dropping the PHP handle may still return the same backend on the next connect.

TX-02.savepoint-rollback-not-sent.reason: PDO has no savepoint or nested-transaction API. PDO::beginTransaction, commit, and rollBack are the transaction API. Issuing SAVEPOINT SQL from this control would be application SQL, not a PDO nested transaction.

TX-02.savepoint-rollback-rejected.reason: PDO has no savepoint or nested-transaction API. PDO::beginTransaction, commit, and rollBack are the transaction API. Issuing SAVEPOINT SQL from this control would be application SQL, not a PDO nested transaction.

TX-02.conn-lost-before-savepoint-rollbac.reason: PDO has no savepoint or nested-transaction API. PDO::beginTransaction, commit, and rollBack are the transaction API. Issuing SAVEPOINT SQL from this control would be application SQL, not a PDO nested transaction.

TX-04.nested-failure-contained.reason: PDO has no nested-transaction or savepoint API. A nested scope cannot be started through PDO.

TX-04.nested-released-outer-rollback.reason: PDO has no nested-transaction or savepoint API. A nested scope cannot be started through PDO.

TX-04.independent-inner.reason: PDO has no propagation mode and no API that commits an inner transaction while an outer transaction stays open. There are no deferred writes. The hazard TX-04.3 targets cannot arise through PDO's transaction API.

TX-05.managed-serializable.reason: PDO::beginTransaction() takes no isolation level. The Pdo\Pgsql::TRANSACTION_* constants are deprecated in PHP 8.5 and have no effect. There is no PDO method that requests SERIALIZABLE. Sending SET TRANSACTION from this control would be PostgreSQL SQL, not a PDO API.

TX-05.explicit-serializable.reason: PDO has no transaction handle distinct from the PDO object, and PDO::beginTransaction() takes no isolation level. The same absence as the managed case.

MG-02.held.reason: PDO has no migration runner, migration history, or multi-process advisory-lock protocol. This adapter does not add one.
